paragraphs: Friend, here's the lesson. Pride sets itself up against the LORD, and it always ends empty. Moab bragged and bragged, and the LORD said, "His boasting is as empty as his deeds" (Jeremiah 48:30). Nobody wins an argument with the One who made them, and I say that as a stamper who once tried to out-brag his own oven.

But listen to the crying. The passage says, "I will wail for Moab" (Jeremiah 48:31), and then the LORD says, "My heart laments like a flute for Moab" (Jeremiah 48:36). Judgment here does not come from a God who enjoys it. I think that's the part to hold onto, friend: the One who brings pride low is the same One who grieves over it.

And then comes the little word that gets me every time: "Yet in the latter days I will restore Moab from captivity," declares the LORD (Jeremiah 48:47). Pride can bring a nation low, but it doesn't get the last word, and for Moab the promised word is restoration. So bring your pride to Him before it breaks, and stay in the Word, because the teaching isn't over.
